raw:
You come down the staff stairs into the foyer as the older man finishes carrying a stack of opening programmes to an empty table.

“I’m Rowan Garvey,” you say. “What’s most urgent before the screening?”

Nell looks up from the office doorway, a paper diary tucked under one arm.

“There isn’t a screening tonight,” she says. “The public reopening starts on Saturday the twenty-sixth. And nothing’s urgent from you this evening. Tomorrow, at nine, we’ll go through the archive procedure and the loan records before you begin handling anything.”

From the kitchen, a woman’s voice carries over the clink of dishes. “What is urgent is that the pie has a short and glorious life outside the oven.”

Nell smiles briefly. “That’s Jo. She has the café concession. Owen’s helping her in the kitchen. This is Martin, Bea, and Rosa.”

The older man gives you a small nod. “Martin. Welcome.”

Rosa, in a paint-flecked navy work jacket, lifts a hand from beside the programmes. “Hi, Rowan.”

Bea sits at the end of the pushed-together tables, sorting cutlery into small, exact piles. “It’s good to meet you properly.”

Nell glances towards the ceiling as another muted electronic tone sounds from the projection booth. “Dev’s upstairs finishing a check. He’ll be down when he can be persuaded food is real.”

Jo emerges through the kitchen door with a broad ceramic dish in both hands. Steam rises from its browned crust. A younger man follows with a salad bowl and sets it down beside the bread.

“Right,” Jo says. “Nobody needs to earn supper. There’s an empty chair there, Rowan.”

The eighth place waits at the table, beside a carton of unopened crockery and within reach of the tomato stew.
